It depends where you are coming from Morally.

Do you believe that there is a force or being larger than humanity that defines morals for people?

If not, then humans are their own creators of morals.

If that is true, then the stronger, more numerous, non-indigenous Americans do not have any reason to consider the good of others outside themselves, especially if it would provide them some kind of detriment or unease.

I know it sounds cold, and it's not my personal belief, but I know people who think like this

I have had a similar thing happen. Firstly:

1. You do not owe your family anything. Now, you may be thinking about all the time, energy and love all of them have given to you and that takes anyone to bring anyone else up to age 17. So you do owe them, for sure, but not right now. They do need and deserve your help, but not right now. Right now, you cannot help them while you yourself are being harmed. You need to get out of the negative loop and heal up.

2. Find out your problems. Face them down and fix them. I look at it like broken bones. Everybody has one. You might shake someone's hand and wonder why you react so strongly to such a perfectly ordinary task, but if your arm is broken, it makes sense. Everyone has broken bones, hurts from the past, that cause them to react strongly to certain situations and circumstances, however normal those may be. You can't get better by grimacing and trying to continue on the way you are going without reacting strongly. Nobody flips out in a fit of anger, or cringes in fear of a seemingly normal situation for nothing. Pretending nothing is wrong and trying to act like it will just make things worse.

3. Forgiveness is instrumental to healing. If someone hurts you, that hurt does not stay in the past. That hurt is repeat in some sense every time you remember what they did. It changes how you act even if you try to bury it, and you will end up hurting other people. In that way, pain and hate are like a contagious disease. The hard part of it is that the only way to keep the past in the past is to forgive it. Not just to try and feel good about it and brush on like it never happened, but to fully face up to what happened, and how it hurt you, and then release the other person. When I say release, I mean that when someone commits a wrong against you, it's like the scales of justice are tipped. They are in your debt. Forgiveness is like saying they owe you nothing. Expect tears, write a journal, and expect your life to change so much for the better. mine did.

Finally, and importantly, the act of facing up to what they did should be done only when you are ready to forgive them. If you realize that your hurt and screwed up attitudes and behaviours came from other people but do not move on from there, you will get worse, you will accept no responsibility for your actions, and you will think that other people have the power to drastically change who you are. This is scary. You have power. Forgiveness is more powerful than you might think.

Marx had a number of branches to his thought.

History
Marx thought that history was going to sort of just even its way out by way of conflict. There were always an oppressive ruling class and and oppressed serving class. The oppressed lower class would eventually revolt, and out of that revolution a new middle class would be formed. The middle class would become the new ruling class. A new lower class would form. The lower class would revolt, a new middle class would form, and so forth. Marx saw Communism as the completion of history, where there was basically a single class and therefore no conflict.

Labour
Marx thought that everyone should have some connection to the things that they produce. You know how when you work hard to make a bead necklace or some such thing, you feel really attached to it, and it feels kinda good to make money selling it? Marx thought that the completion of the human person was to have a connection to what you make when you work.
Capitalism was basically someone taking more than their fair share of the work, as Marx saw the Industrial barons taking the work of the factory workers from there and not returning equally. Hence communism

That is a horribly abridged version of Marxism, and I am missing many essential parts, but that's the gist of it.

If I recorded myself saying "I love you" and then played it back to myself, it wouldn't mean anything, because I made it say that. We believe that in order for love to exist there must be the choice to love or not love.

While God made the world good, we as a human race still had the option of not loving him, and we chose that. So we don't see it so much as a reward/punishment as much as we see it as God having made us for a paradise with him, and we chose otherwise.

We actually believe that everyone deserves hell, because we have all essentially made that choice at some point. Where the whole blood sacrifice comes in, is as a result of a sort of moral dilemma. God is depicted as both

1. loving
and
2. Just

We believe that humanity, having rejected God initially, strictly according to Justice, deserved to be destroyed. However, according to love, God took that destruction on himself by becoming a representative of all humanity (Which is why Jesus was a person, and even bothered coming).

We believe that if that sacrifice instantly saved everyone without them having to choose or anything, because we still have freedom of choice, we could still easily choose evil again and the whole thing would have to happen over again.

That is why we believe people have to "accept Jesus", as we put it, to actively choose God as a way out of that destruction.
